Claude Code Environment Variables: A Complete Reference Guide
Environment variables are configuration values that live outside your code, typically set at the system or application level.
They’re a standard way to configure applications without hardcoding sensitive data or deployment-specific settings.
For Claude Code, you don’t need to configure these variables to get started. The defaults work great.
However, knowing they exist is valuable, when you need enterprise deployments, performance optimization, or cloud integrations, you’ll know exactly where to look.
Authentication and API
Configure authentication methods for Claude Code.
These variables control API keys, authorization tokens, and custom headers used when communicating with Anthropic’s services or AWS Bedrock.
Model Configuration
Control which Claude models are used for different tasks. Configure model aliases (sonnet, opus, haiku) and specify models for subagents.
These settings determine the AI model behavior and capabilities for your Claude Code instance.
Bash and Command Execution
Manage how Claude Code executes bash commands.
Set timeouts for long-running commands, control output length limits, and configure working directory behavior to optimize command execution in your workflow.
Cloud Infrastructure (Bedrock/Vertex)
Enable and configure cloud platform integrations.
Use these variables to connect Claude Code with AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex AI, configure regional deployments, and manage authentication for cloud-based model access.
MCP (Model Context Protocol)
Configure MCP server behavior.
Control timeouts for server startup and tool execution, and set limits on output token size to manage MCP server performance and resource usage.
Proxy and Network
Configure network proxy settings for corporate environments.
Set HTTP/HTTPS proxy servers and define exceptions for domains that should bypass the proxy, enabling Claude Code to work behind corporate firewalls.
Security and Certificates
Set up mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication for enhanced security.
Configure client certificates, private keys, and passphrases required for secure communication in enterprise environments with strict security requirements.
Telemetry and Debugging
Control data collection and reporting features. Disable telemetry, error reporting, automatic updates, and debug commands.
These settings help maintain privacy and control over what data is shared with Anthropic’s services.
UX and Behavior
Customize the user experience and interface behavior.
Control terminal title updates, cost warnings, non-essential model calls, and IDE extension installations to tailor Claude Code’s behavior to your preferences.
Optimization and Performance
Fine-tune performance and resource usage.
Configure output token limits, enable extended thinking, control prompt caching per model, and optimize tools like ripgrep. These settings help balance performance, cost, and quality.
Advanced Configuration
Advanced settings for specialized use cases.
These settings are typically used in enterprise environments with custom authentication requirements.
